title: Common K-flat model for integral quotient pullback faces
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and $n\geq1$. On the small pro-étale site of each scheme $T$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention] put $R_T=p_T^*\underline A=\varprojlim_{m\geq1}(A/\pi^m)_T$, $S_T=(A/\pi^n)_T$, and let $a_T:R_T\to S_T$ be the actual finite projection [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit]. Regard these also as their reconstructed section-ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence].

Let $X'\xrightarrow{h} X$, $Y'\xrightarrow{g}Y$, $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$ be a chosen cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. For an edge $u:U\to V$, use ordinary section-module pullback $p^B_u$ and its unbounded derived functor $L^B_u$ for $B=R,S$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Write $t_T(P)=P\otimes_{R_T}S_T$ for termwise sheafified scalar extension, $T_T=-\otimes^L_{R_T}S_T$ for its uncompleted derived functor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and $Q$ for localization from cochain complexes to the ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\chi_u:L^S_uT_V\xrightarrow\sim T_UL^R_u$ be the canonical ringed scalar/pullback comparison normalized by the balanced map $u^{-1}(x\otimes s)\mapsto u^{-1}x\otimes u^{-1}s$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback, lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization]. Let $\vartheta^B:L^B_{f'}L^B_g\xrightarrow\sim L^B_hL^B_f$ be the geometric square built from the specified composition maps [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition].

The canonical coefficient identifications $c_{u,R}:u^{-1}R_V\cong R_U$ and $c_{u,S}:u^{-1}S_V\cong S_U$ [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] satisfy $a_Uc_{u,R}=c_{u,S}u^{-1}a_V$, commute with identities and composition, and agree with the pulled-back condensed coefficient identifications after every finite projection.

Every $M\in D(R_Y)$ admits a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution, def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For every such $P$, all intermediate ordinary complexes in the routes
$$p^S_{f'}p^S_gt_YP\longrightarrow p^S_{f'}t_{Y'}p^R_gP\longrightarrow t_{X'}p^R_{f'}p^R_gP\longrightarrow t_{X'}p^R_hp^R_fP$$
and
$$p^S_{f'}p^S_gt_YP\longrightarrow p^S_hp^S_ft_YP\longrightarrow p^S_ht_Xp^R_fP\longrightarrow t_{X'}p^R_hp^R_fP$$
are K-flat with flat terms over their current ring. Under the canonical representative identifications $L^B_uQ(P')\cong Q(p^B_uP')$ and $T_TQ(P')\cong Q(t_TP')$, the six derived faces $L^S_{f'}(\chi_g)$, $\chi_{f'}L^R_g$, $T_{X'}(\vartheta^R)$, $\vartheta^ST_Y$, $L^S_h(\chi_f)$, $\chi_hL^R_f$ are the localizations of the respective ordinary faces in these two routes on this same $P$. The ordinary scalar faces are the stated balanced-generator maps and the ordinary square faces are the geometric inverse-image compositors. These representative identifications and face formulas are natural for chain maps between flat-term K-flat representatives. No flatness of $a_T$, boundedness, properness or completeness is assumed.

proof.text: Use the quotient condensed-ring map $\underline A\to\underline{A/\pi^n}$ defining the actual projection, with index $n-1$ in the zero-based notation of [def-sfb-integral-quotient-coefficients]. The coefficient maps $c_{u,R},c_{u,S}$ are the components at these two rings of the same natural isomorphism $u^{-1}p_V^*\cong p_U^*$ of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp, sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]. Its naturality at this quotient map says precisely $a_Uc_{u,R}=c_{u,S}u^{-1}a_V$. The integral-limit description of [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit] is the canonical identification of this pulled-back ring with its finite quotient limit. To check the projection normalization, use [lem-sfb-finite-reduction-pullback] at any positive exponent $m$: its hypothesis holds because the actual quotient map sends every continuous $b:H\to A$ to $b\bmod\pi^m$, hence its adjunction mate is the relative finite-label map $T[b\bmod\pi^m]$. Its conclusion gives the identical square with $a_m$ and the finite coefficient identification. This is a separate check at each $m$; it does not assert that inverse image preserves an infinite limit.

proof.text: The same coefficient identifications have the required identity and composition laws. Indeed [lem-sfb-eta-id] identifies the adjunct of the identity coefficient map with the pushforward unitor. For composable edges, [lem-sfb-eta-comp] identifies the adjunct of the composite coefficient map with the two successive adjuncts and the pushforward compositor. Apply the adjunction bijections to these equations: the pasting law of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] identifies their transposes with respectively the pullback unitor and $c_{v,B}\circ v^{-1}(c_{u,B})$ after the geometric compositor, for $B=R,S$. Injectivity of these bijections gives the identity and composition laws for $c$. Since the argument uses the natural coefficient identifications of Step 1, the laws also hold after every finite projection.

Represent $M$ by a complex $K$ and apply [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] to obtain a quasi-isomorphism $P\to K$ with $P$ K-flat and each term flat. Fix any flat-term K-flat $P$, as required by the universal assertion in the statement. Each $p_u^B$ is pullback for the ringed geometric morphism with structural map $c_{u,B}$. Each $t_T$ is pullback for the identity geometric morphism with structural map $a_T:R_T\to S_T$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] applies to both kinds of edge, including the nonflat quotient edge. Induct on the length of any of the finitely many words displayed in the statement: the length-zero word is $P$; applying its last edge preserves both K-flatness and flatness of all terms. Consequently every intermediate complex in both routes has these properties over its current ring. This is flatness over $S_T$ after quotient extension, and does not assert flatness over $R_T$ of the restricted quotient.

For a flat-term K-flat intermediate $P'$, take the universal cochain computation counit $\epsilon^B_{u,P'}:L_u^BQ(P')\to Q(p_u^BP')$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], which is invertible and natural in chain maps. Take also the scalar computation $\epsilon^a_{T,P'}:T_TQ(P')\to Q(t_TP')$ of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Starting at the input, whisker and compose these counits in the order of each word. Step 3 ensures that every next component is invertible. This gives the canonical representative identifications at every vertex of both routes, with no second resolution. The naturality clauses of these two cited computation results give naturality of all these composites on chain maps.

Use Step 1 to identify the target rings with $u^{-1}R_V,u^{-1}S_V$. Under this identification the ordinary scalar face is exactly the invertible coequalizer comparison $\chi_u^{\mathrm{ord}}$ of [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization]. In the right-tensor convention of the item it sends the inverse image of $x\otimes s$ to the inverse image of $x$ tensored with the inverse image of $s$, with the coefficient transported by $c_{u,S}$. This formula is balanced: replacing $rx\otimes s$ by $x\otimes a_V(r)s$ yields the same target by $a_Uc_{u,R}=c_{u,S}u^{-1}a_V$ from Step 1. It respects restrictions and addition, so it defines the sheafified tensor map. The tensor universal property in [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus] makes these generator formulas determining; no assumption that every sheaf section is pure is used. The normalization theorem says that, under Step 4's computation counits, $Q(\chi_u^{\mathrm{ord}})^{-1}$ is the scalar-adjunction mate. Hence $Q(\chi_u^{\mathrm{ord}})$ represents the canonical $\chi_u$ in the direction specified by this item. This also specifies the scalar/pullback comparison that the tensor-pullback citation in the imported statement alone did not state.

For $B=R,S$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] to the two length-two paths from $X'$ to $Y$. Their ring identifications agree by Step 2 and the chosen cartesian identification $gf'=fh$. The cited comparison is computed on flat-term K-flat complexes by the termwise geometric module-pullback compositor. Therefore $\vartheta^B=(c^B_{h,f})\circ(c^B_{f',g})^{-1}$, with the middle composite identified using $gf'=fh$, is represented by the corresponding composite of ordinary compositors. In particular the ordinary square faces act only by the geometric inverse-image identifications and the coefficient transport already fixed in Step 2. For the $S$ square its input is $t_YP$, which is flat-term K-flat over $S_Y$ by Step 3; for the $R$ square its input is $P$.

Apply [lem-trf-ringed-kflat-word-comparison-descent] to the finite collection of ringed topoi $(T,R_T),(T,S_T)$ for the four vertices, the eight geometric pullbacks and the four identity-topos scalar edges. These are morphisms of small-site ringed topoi by the size convention in the statement; all structural maps are ring maps and the quotient squares commute by Step 1. The derived edge counits are exactly Step 4's normalized ones. The theorem's representative equation and its preservation of whiskering give the following six ordinary representatives, in order: $p^S_{f'}(\chi_g^{\mathrm{ord}})$, $\chi_{f'}^{\mathrm{ord}}p_g^R$, $t_{X'}(\vartheta^{R,\mathrm{ord}})$, $\vartheta^{S,\mathrm{ord}}t_Y$, $p_h^S(\chi_f^{\mathrm{ord}})$, and $\chi_h^{\mathrm{ord}}p_f^R$. Steps 5 and 6 identify their unwhiskered derived transformations with the prescribed $\chi$ and $\vartheta$. The representative equation therefore identifies precisely the six faces in the statement, using the common vertex identifications of Step 4. In particular applying $T_{X'}$ to the $R$ square is computed by the ordinary $t_{X'}$ on that square, because both its endpoints are flat-term K-flat.

Finally let $b:P\to\widetilde P$ be a chain map between flat-term K-flat representatives. All vertex comparison maps are natural by Step 4. Each ordinary scalar face is a natural transformation on module sheaves, so its degreewise formula commutes with $b$; the same holds for the geometric compositors of Step 6. Applying $Q$ and the whiskered representative equations of Step 7 gives the asserted chain-map naturality of all six face formulas. Every operation used is termwise additive and every face has degree zero, so the argument applies to arbitrary unbounded cochain complexes without additional signs. Together with Steps 1-3 this proves every clause, without properness or completeness assumptions.
